title: Kingdom of Hawaï'i
capsule: The Hawaiian Kingdom was unified by Kamehameha I between 1795 and 1810, when he brought all major islands under a single monarchy, establishing Honolulu as the effective capital. The kingdom maintained formal diplomatic recognition from the United States, Britain, and France, signed commercial treaties, and developed a constitutional government from 1840; it was one of the few Pacific states to achieve this level of international standing. On 17 January 1893 a group of American sugar planters and US Marines overthrew Queen Liliuokalani; the Republic of Hawaii was declared in 1894, and the islands were formally annexed by the United States in 1898 under the Newlands Resolution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Hawaiian Kingdom's territorial extent (the main archipelago) is precisely known; its political and diplomatic history from 1795 to 1893 is exceptionally well documented by royal archives and US State Department records.
